newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Brash signs fresh agreement with new NZ government.
newsitem.headline: Brash signs fresh agreement with new NZ government.

text.p: Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash confirmed on Tuesday that he had signed a new Policy Targets Agreement (PTA) with Finance Minister Bill Birch.

"The widening of the inflation target to zero to three percent, and the amendment to Clause 1 of the Policy Targets Agreement, as announced earlier by (Treasurer Winston) Mr Peters, are fully consistent with the requirements and intent of the Reserve Bank Act," Brash said in a statement. "Acccordingly, I am happy to work with the new PTA," Brash said.
Birch earlier said Brash would remain as RBNZ governor.
He also said underlying inflation could move outside the zero to three percent band in response to shocks. The previous agreement was for a zero to two percent range.
"In the event of such shocks, the bank will be fully accountable for its handling of price effects and, in particular, for any movements outside the zero to three percent band," Birch said.

The agreement now requires the bank to formulate and implement monetary policy with "the intention of maintaining stability in the general level of prices, so that monetary policy can make its maximum contribution to sustainable growth, employment and development opportunities", Birch said.
